narrative.overview:
The campaign is drawn as a São Paulo-style metro line. Graphite sign bars carry the name and the countdown; a red route strip runs under them; every day with activity is a station on a vertical red line that ends at a double-ringed terminal on election day. The interface reads like wayfinding signage, not like a calendar app: condensed uppercase station names, tabular condensed times, round line bullets, and two line weights only (the 8px route and 1px seams).

Density is phone-first and generous. Tap targets are 44 to 48px, the ground is a pale platform grey so white panels separate without heavy shadows, and contrast holds up outdoors. On desktop the same world becomes a production bench: line on the left, a persistent share bench on the right. The ten 1080 × 1350 flyer layouts are the same signage at poster scale, each a different object from the metro (a station sign, a departures board, a ticket, a tile wall, a network map), so a shared image and the site are recognisably one system. The brand is a red calendar mark beside the name, in the sign bar, the favicon and every flyer.

The world explicitly refuses the default calendar app (white cards on white, grid first) and the protest-poster costume (cream paper with condensed ink boxes).
keyCharacteristics: One red route line (8px) is the spine of every view; flyers carry route red as a scaled line, a strip or a full ground.
Platform yellow appears only on the next station.
Activity types are other metro line colours, shown as round bullets and named once.
Barlow for reading, Barlow Condensed for signs, times and dates.
Flat panels outlined by a 1px seam ring; 6px rectangular corners.
The line draws itself once on load, along its own axis.
The brand is a red calendar mark; station rings stay rings and are never the logo.

rules.name: The Reserved Yellow Rule
rules.body: Platform yellow marks the next station and nothing else. A focus ring on dark surfaces is the only other use.

rules.name: The Two Reserved Colours Rule
rules.body: Route red and platform yellow never appear among the activity-type colours. Types ride the connection-line palette only.

rules.name: The Travelled Line Rule
rules.body: Time already behind today turns the line and its rings to `travelled` grey, and past text to muted ink. Never hide past stations; grey them.

rules.name: The Flyer Palette Rule
rules.body: Flyers use route red, graphite, the connection lines and white or pale neutrals, nothing else. Platform yellow never appears on a flyer. The few material neutrals a layout needs (tile white and grout, flap-tile grey, pasted-paper white) belong to the object it depicts.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, date and count is set in Barlow Condensed with tabular figures, so the time column aligns like a departures board.

rules.name: The Said Once Rule
rules.body: A type is named in exactly one place per item, next to its bullet. Nothing is labelled twice.

rules.name: The Poster Scale Rule
rules.body: Flyer sizes (24 to 520px) belong to the flyer scale and never enter the UI ramp. A flyer's title takes one of four size classes picked from text length (is-xl, is-lg, is-md, is-sm), never a hand-tuned size.

rules.name: The Seam Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Panels are separated by a 1px seam ring, not by drop shadows. Only floating surfaces, and the depicted objects on a flyer, get a soft lift.

rules.name: The Two Line Weights Rule
rules.body: In the interface, lines come in two weights only: the 8px route and the 1px seam. Selection and active states use the route colour at 2 to 4px as an inset (tab underline, selected month day), never a third decorative stroke. Flyers scale the route and may draw the edges of the object they depict (ticket perforation, enamel frieze trim, departures-board row rules, interchange outline), but no decorative borders.

rules.name: The Mark Is Not A Ring Rule
rules.body: The logo is the calendar mark. Station rings, terminals and type bullets are line vocabulary and never stand in for the brand.

dos: Do keep the 8px route red line as the spine of any new view or export; red stays dominant through the line and the primary action, not through filled areas.
Do set all times, dates and counts in Barlow Condensed with tabular figures.
Do separate panels with the 1px seam ring on platform grey (`0 0 0 1px` seam plus a 1 to 2px drop).
Do show an activity type as a round line bullet plus its name, once per item, using only the connection-line palette.
Do keep tap targets at 44px or more and primary buttons at 48px.
Do grey out time that has passed (travelled line, muted text) rather than removing it.
Do put the brand (calendar mark and name) and the slogan on every flyer, with the slogan beside the contact or link when they exist.
Do make each new flyer layout a real object from the metro (a sign, a board, a ticket, a wall, a map) built from the shared brand, type mark and footer, with its title sized by the length classes.
donts: Don't use platform yellow for anything but the next station (and focus rings on dark surfaces).
Don't give an activity type route red or platform yellow.
Don't add a third line weight or decorative border; the system has the 8px route and the 1px seam.

Don't drift into the default calendar app look (white cards on white, grid as the first view) or the protest-poster costume (cream paper, condensed ink boxes) in the interface. Lambe-lambe is the one flyer that quotes pasted street posters, and it stays inside the palette.
Don't label a type or a station twice.
Don't use a ring or a disc as the logo, and don't bring flyer sizes into the UI ramp.
